legal_rules_infrastructure.detail: Governed Ruleset/Rule/Source/TestCase/EngineRun schema and lifecycle (src-tauri/src/legal_rules.rs), a constrained-DSL rule interpreter (10 safe operators, no code eval/network/filesystem), and a Settings UI for authoring/testing/approving rulesets. Contains zero Israeli substantive law - a ruleset is only usable once a lawyer has sourced, tested and approved it. Phase B (Medical/Wage/Liability evidence ledgers) and Phase C (the first real lawyer-approved legal module) are deliberately not attempted.

legal_rules_infrastructure_hardening.detail: All 6 P0 findings and 5 of 6 P1 findings from the 2026-08-25 independent audit fixed and covered by new regression tests: terminal-state immutability (approved/superseded/revoked, not just approved), required non-empty reviewer identity on approve/review, page-level (not version-level) source grounding for approval, engine_kind always read from the ruleset itself, effective-period validation and enforcement, deterministic priority/rule_key tie-breaking, atomic single-transaction approval, forward-only engine-run status, exact integer arithmetic for cent-valued comparisons, and rejection of meaningless (assertion-free) test cases. P1-6 (linking legal_engine_runs to legal_deadlines/damage_calculations via FK) is deliberately deferred until real integration work begins, per the audit's own recommendation. cargo test --locked: 58/58 at the time; confirmed on real Windows CI at run #14, commit d7b3ae6.

phase_b_matter_profile.detail: First milestone (B1) of the Phase B roadmap: a matter_profile 1:1 side table and a matter_parties contact list, plus a Rust-side allowlist tightening create_matter/update_matter's case type. The existing matters table is never ALTERed - src-tauri/src/matter_profile.rs and its migration explain why. Plain office-management data: no lock/approval lifecycle, no DB immutability triggers, since none of it is an evidentiary claim. The original shape (event_date/court_name/a single contact_details blob, case types motor_vehicle_accident/workplace_accident/.../generic_civil) was confirmed on real Windows CI at run #15, commit 16a31b3. A design review then prompted fixes applied in place (before any client-use database depended on the original shape): event_date/court_name renamed to primary_event_date/primary_court_name (room for a matter's many dates/proceedings); contact_details replaced with structured display_name/entity_kind/identifier/phone/email/address fields; the case-type taxonomy renamed/widened to traffic_accident/work_accident/general_negligence/medical_malpractice/civil_commercial/generic_civil/other (generic_civil kept for backward compatibility); matter_parties.role's DB CHECK dropped in favor of Rust-only validation. This review-fix commit (6e89cd0) was confirmed on real Windows CI at run #16 - 66/66 tests passed on the real runner. B2-B6 (Workstreams, Missing Evidence Matrix, Medical/Wage/Liability Ledgers, AI Pipeline, Case Health) remain deliberately unattempted - each gets its own planning pass before implementation; the review also refined that roadmap (B5 splits into B5a focused-retrieval before B5b AI-ledger-proposals; B3's requirements read as office-policy, not statutory; B4's ledger items use a draft/verified/superseded/stale lifecycle) without changing any shipped code.

phase_b_workstreams.detail: Second milestone (B2) of the Phase B roadmap: a matter_workstreams table (medical/liability/wage/insurance/btl/negotiation/litigation, each not_applicable/not_started/active/blocked/done) auto-seeded from a matter's case type at creation via a new workstreams::reconcile function, called inside the same transaction as create_matter's INSERT (now wrapped in conn.transaction() for the first time) and update_matter's UPDATE when matterType actually changes (update_matter now SELECTs the old value first to detect a real change). reconcile is idempotent and non-destructive: it inserts any of the 7 kinds not yet present, then upgrades an existing not_applicable row to not_started only if the new case type's defaults include it - an already not_started/active/blocked/done workstream is never touched. list_matter_workstreams calls reconcile first (read-repair) before listing, so a pre-B2 matter with zero workstream rows gets backfilled transparently on first view. Kind/status are Rust-only validated (no DB CHECK), matching matter_profile.rs's own pattern. Matter Pack defaults are office-workflow defaults, not legal determinations - freely overridable per matter. New tab 'מסלולי עבודה' in MatterWorkspace.tsx (WorkstreamsTab.tsx); a case-type <select> was added to the existing edit-matter modal so a lawyer can actually trigger a case-type change. 9 new backend tests (seeding, reconcile-never-touches-active, backfill-on-list, kind/status validation, cascade delete, plus 3 pure unit tests) - 75/75 total. cargo check/test --locked, npm run build, contract:check (94/94, no drift), qa:static (now also checking oneTableInMatterWorkstreams) all pass. Migration re-verified idempotent via direct sqlite3 (applied 3x): 41 tables, 28 indexes, 37 triggers, user_version=15, integrity ok, fk_check clean. Confirmed on real Windows CI at run #17 (https://github.com/yossizch-max/-2/actions/runs/32926614574), commit 0be99a9 - 75/75 tests passed on the real runner. B3-B6 remain deliberately unattempted, each still pending its own planning pass.

phase_b_requirements.detail: Third milestone (B3) of the Phase B roadmap: a matter_requirements checklist table (13 typical document keys - id_document/police_report/medical_records_initial/medical_records_full_file/wage_stubs/employer_incident_report/witness_statements/insurance_policy/btl_forms/vehicle_photos/expert_opinion/contract_document/correspondence_records - each not_applicable/not_collected/requested/collected/stale) built to the exact same shape and reconcile idiom as B2's matter_workstreams: one idempotent, non-destructive requirements::reconcile function called from create_matter, from update_matter on a real case-type change, and as read-repair in list_matter_requirements. Deliberately no linked_document_id column in this pass - wiring a requirement to a specific document (an 'open source' button, a staleness cascade off scanner.rs) has no consumer yet and would be a speculative, unused column; status stays entirely lawyer-driven, including 'stale', since what that should mean for a checklist item isn't yet defined by real usage. New tab 'ראיות חסרות' in MatterWorkspace.tsx (MissingEvidenceTab.tsx), structurally identical to WorkstreamsTab.tsx. The original shape (86/86 tests) was shipped at commit 94f7c63. A user code review then found a genuine semantic gap: priority was computed only from the matter's current case-type Pack, so a requirement the lawyer manually collected outside the Pack (or one whose Pack membership changed after collection) could surface as status=collected next to priority=not_applicable - a self-contradictory read, even though the underlying reconcile/status-preservation logic never touched the row incorrectly. Fixed in place (no migration - schema unchanged, still user_version=16/42 tables/29 indexes/37 triggers) by splitting the read-model into two fields, both still computed at read time and never persisted: relevance (applicable/not_applicable - whether the key currently belongs to the Pack, or the lawyer has otherwise acted on it) and priority (required_by_office_policy/recommended/optional - only meaningful when relevant, Option<String> now instead of overloading not_applicable as if it were a priority tier). A key in the current Pack keeps the Pack's priority; a key outside the Pack still at status=not_applicable is relevance=not_applicable/priority=None; a key outside the Pack that the lawyer has moved to not_collected/requested/collected/stale becomes relevance=applicable/priority=optional, so a lawyer's own action never produces a contradictory display again. 3 new tests (2 unit tests on the split function, 1 integration regression test reproducing the exact reported scenario) plus updated assertions on the existing seeding test - 89/89 total. cargo check/test --locked, npm run build, contract:check (96/96, no drift), qa:static all pass. linked_document_id and manual-only stale remain deliberately deferred, reaffirmed by the same review as still correct. The original B3 commit (94f7c63) was confirmed on real Windows CI at run #18 (https://github.com/yossizch-max/-2/actions/runs/32929039159) - 86/86 tests passed on the real runner. This review-fix commit was confirmed at run #19 (https://github.com/yossizch-max/-2/actions/runs/32930093339) - 89/89 tests passed on the real runner. B4-B6 remain deliberately unattempted, each still pending its own planning pass.

phase_b_ledgers.detail: Fourth milestone (B4) of the Phase B roadmap: three parallel per-matter ledgers - medical_events, wage_records, liability_facts (named/framed as grounded facts bearing on liability, not a legal determination TAHRIR asserts) - each with its own source-grounding child table copying legal_authorities/legal_authority_passages' verbatim-containment-checked, hash-chained shape (composite FOREIGN KEY(entry_id,matter_id) REFERENCES <table>(id,matter_id), this schema's standard cross-matter-leak guard). Lifecycle is draft -> verified with correction-by-supersession, not authorities.rs's terminal-only verified: a correction never mutates the old verified row, it INSERTs a brand-new row whose supersedes_entry_id points back at the old one (a composite self-FK, structurally blocking cross-matter supersession); 'is this entry superseded' is computed at read time (does some OTHER VERIFIED row point at me?) - a pending, unverified draft correction deliberately does not yet mark the old entry superseded. verify_entry requires at least one source (fails closed) and re-checks verbatim containment fresh against each source's current page text right before flipping status, mirroring authorities::verify/legal_rules::approve_ruleset/ai::approve_proposal's recheck-at-terminal-transition discipline. A verified entry's fields are made immutable via a BEFORE UPDATE trigger; its sources get matching BEFORE INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE triggers (closing a gap legal_authority_passages itself has, left unaddressed there). One shared Rust engine (ledger.rs, a LedgerKind enum dispatching table names) implements add_source/verify_entry/list_entry_sources/supersession-validation generically across all three kinds; each kind gets its own small typed create/update_draft/list functions and models.rs struct. New 'פנקסים' tab in MatterWorkspace.tsx (LedgersTab.tsx: three sections, each with a creation/correction form, a source-attachment control reusing the document/page-picker pattern from AuthoritiesTab.tsx, and verify/correct actions). No AI-proposal integration in this pass - deliberately deferred to B5b per the already-agreed roadmap, which writes into these same tables once it lands. The original shape (commit 7bdb60a, 103/103 tests) shipped with 5 gaps a user code review then found before any Windows CI run confirmed it, all fixed in place in the same migration/module: (1) a verified entry/source could be deleted directly via SQL - fixed with a ledger_delete_guard control table gating the delete-blocking triggers, so only a deliberate whole-matter cascade wrapped in ledger::with_cascade_delete_guard can remove a verified row; (2) the stale carve-out on the update trigger was bidirectional - fixed to allow only 0->1, never resetting a verified row's stale flag back to trustworthy without a fresh supersession; (3) verify_entry never checked document_versions.stale, so a draft could verify against a source whose document had already changed underneath it - fixed by joining document_versions and rejecting a stale source at verify time, mirroring ai::approve_proposal's own re-check; (4) nothing stopped two independent draft corrections of the same verified entry from both becoming verified successors - fixed with a Rust pre-check plus a partial UNIQUE(matter_id,supersedes_entry_id) WHERE status='verified' index as the DB-level backstop; (5) integrity_sha256 hashed only entry_id+source hashes, not the entry's own domain fields - fixed with a generic per-row column snapshot (via rusqlite ValueRef, no per-kind knowledge needed) folded into the hash alongside each source's page id/version id/hash. 6 new/updated tests (unguarded-delete-rejected, guarded-cascade-still-succeeds, stale-cannot-reset-to-0, verify-rejects-a-stale-source-version, only-one-verified-successor, hash-reflects-domain-fields) plus the original 14 (draft create/edit, containment rejection, verify-requires-a-source, re-check-at-verify-time, verified-immutability, source-immutability, supersession lifecycle including the pending-draft-correction case, cross-matter-supersession-blocked, cascade-delete-even-when-verified, plus 2 pure unit tests on LedgerKind) plus one existing scanner test extended for the stale-cascade - 106/106 total. cargo check/test --locked, npm run build, contract:check (106/106, no drift), qa:static (now checking sevenTablesInMatterLedgers, since ledger_delete_guard is a 7th table in this migration) all pass. Migration re-verified idempotent via direct sqlite3 (applied 3x): 49 tables, 35 indexes, 52 triggers, user_version=17 (unchanged - edited in place before B4's own CI run confirmed the original shape), integrity ok, fk_check clean. The original B4 commit (7bdb60a) was confirmed on real Windows CI at run #20 (https://github.com/yossizch-max/-2/actions/runs/32932125926) - 103/103 tests passed on the real runner. This hardening-fix commit (55616b9) was confirmed at run #21 (https://github.com/yossizch-max/-2/actions/runs/32933104625) - 106/106 tests passed on the real runner. B4 is now fully CI-confirmed. B5-B6 remain deliberately unattempted, each still pending its own planning pass.

phase_b_retrieval.detail: Fifth milestone (B5a) of the Phase B roadmap: a pure retrieval-infrastructure pass, no ledger writes, no embeddings, local-first. Replaces ai.rs::plan_context's old flat 'query the 80 most recent non-stale pages' behavior (capability accepted but never used to filter anything) with a real, auditable retrieval pipeline in a new src-tauri/src/retrieval.rs module. Migration 007_retrieval_context_v18.sql adds a local FTS5 index (document_pages_fts) over document_pages.normalized_text, kept in sync via 3 triggers on document_pages (insert/update-of-normalized_text/delete - the delete trigger alone correctly handles cascaded deletes too, since SQLite fires a child row's own triggers even for an ON DELETE CASCADE, verified empirically during the B4 hardening pass) plus one idempotent, incremental backfill statement for every document_pages row that predates the migration. rusqlite 0.37 has no fts5 Cargo feature - FTS5 is already compiled into the bundled SQLCipher build this project uses; this is confirmed at runtime, not assumed, by a permanent fts5_is_available_in_this_sqlite_build test that runs on every cargo test --locked including real Windows CI. Free text is never handed raw to MATCH - compile_fts_query tokenizes on non-alphanumeric boundaries (Unicode-aware, Hebrew/Arabic pass through with no special-casing), phrase-quotes each term (embedded quotes escaped by doubling) and OR-joins them, so FTS5 query-syntax operators a lawyer might type (quotes/AND/OR/NOT/parens/NEAR/*/^) can never be interpreted as query syntax; unicode61 remove_diacritics 2 is documented honestly as Latin-diacritic-only, not a Hebrew nikud/stemming claim. Ranking is an explicit deterministic sort tuple - bm25 ascending, category-boosted as a tie-break only (can never outrank a real text match), version recency, page_number, block_index, source_id - never a blended arbitrary-scale score. matter_id and document_versions.stale=0 are re-applied against the live document_pages/document_versions tables at every stage, including neighbor expansion, never trusted from the FTS index. For each of the top-10 ranked anchor_kind='page' candidates, adjacent page_number-1/+1 rows are pulled live and tagged includedVia:'neighbor' plus neighborOfSourceId recording which anchor pulled them in. A source at or under 8,000 chars is always sent whole; a larger single-row anchor_kind='document' source (a large DOCX/TXT) is never dropped for exceeding the budget - it is deterministically windowed to 4,000 chars, centered on the first char-index match of any query term (or start-of-text with no query), with windowStart/windowEnd/windowSha256 recorded alongside the source's real, unchanged sourceId/textSha256 for the full original text; approve_proposal's existing re-validation still checks the live full source, never the window. Budget enforcement is char-based (walking the deterministic candidate+neighbor order, including what fits, skipping what doesn't while still trying smaller sources after it), not row-count-based. ContextManifest carries a canonical, non-circular manifest_sha256 (hashed over a payload type with no hash field of its own, so identical inputs on the same DB always produce a byte-identical hash across runs); ai_runs.context_manifest_sha256 now reuses this same hash directly instead of computing a second, redundant one, and ai_proposals.source_manifest_json now stores the entire ContextManifest (what was allowed and sent), not just the sources array (structured_json.sourceIds already records what the model cited - a genuinely different thing). Both plan_ai_context (preview) and run_ai_capability (the real run) thread an optional query payload field to the same underlying retrieval::build_context_manifest call, so preview and the real run can never diverge onto different candidate sets. capability_profile is the extension point for B5b but this milestone deliberately only populates extract_facts (today's one real capability, default_query: None - general fact-extraction has no natural keyword focus, so with no explicit query it honestly degrades to the old recency-ordered candidate list) - no placeholder entries for capabilities B5b hasn't designed yet. FactsAITab.tsx gained one optional free-text query input ('מיקוד לחיפוש') wired through to run_ai_capability. A first planning pass on this milestone was sent back with 8 real defects plus 2 scope adjustments before any code was written (the fts5 Cargo-feature misunderstanding, a missing-backfill gap, a naive shadow-table-count assertion, unsafe raw-MATCH query construction, an overclaimed Hebrew-nikud handling claim, a 'drop oversized sources' policy replaced with deterministic windowing, a circular manifest-hash bug, a thinner audit trail, preview/run divergence, and B5b content leaking into a B5a-scoped milestone) - every point is reflected in the shipped design above, not the original draft. 10 new integration tests (cross-matter isolation, stale exclusion even when it would rank first, relevance-beats-recency, neighbor expansion with correct neighborOfSourceId, oversized-document windowing that is never skipped plus deterministic across runs, full-pipeline determinism, char-based budget enforcement, empty/no-match behavior, every manifest source resolves to a real live page, preview/run parity) plus 8 new unit tests in retrieval.rs (ranking tie-break rules, FTS query compilation incl. Hebrew/Arabic/quotes/parens/embedded-quote-escaping, deterministic windowing) - 127/127 total. cargo check/test --locked, npm run build, contract:check (106/106, no drift - only new optional payload fields, no new commands), qa:static (now also checking migration 007's virtual table/sync-triggers/idempotent-backfill and that retrieval.rs never MATCHes a raw, uncompiled query) all pass. Migration re-verified idempotent via direct sqlite3 (applied 3x): 49 real application tables + 6 FTS5 shadow tables, 35 indexes, 55 triggers, user_version=18, integrity ok, fk_check clean; insert/update/direct-delete/cascade-delete-via-matter sync and post-migration backfill of pre-existing rows were all verified against a live in-memory DB, not merely asserted. This commit has not yet had its own Windows CI run. B5b (AI Autopilot -> Ledger Proposals) and B6 (Case Health) remain deliberately unattempted, each still pending its own planning pass.
